Read the current rules from the Pakistan Bar Council and your provincial bar council, and keep the website factual and restrained.

Q: What should a law firm website include?
A: Most firms need a home page, one page per practice area, advocate profiles with enrolment and courts, an about page, general guides, a contact page with address and map, and a privacy notice and disclaimer. Every claim should be factual and checked against current bar council rules before publishing.

Q: Should a law firm website show success rates?
A: Avoid it. Success rates are hard to prove, can mislead because every case is different, and may conflict with professional conduct rules. Describe instead the types of matters you handle, courts where you appear, years of practice and languages spoken, which clients can verify for themselves.

Q: How can a law firm website protect confidential information?
A: Keep enquiry forms short, warn visitors not to send confidential facts until the firm agrees to act, send submissions to a firm email with two-step login, use HTTPS on every page and avoid storing submissions longer than needed. Run conflict checks before discussing any details.

Q: Do legal articles help a law firm get clients?
A: They can, when written as general information rather than advice. Clear, dated explanations of common processes help people find your firm in search and show expertise. Review them when the law changes, mark them as general information and invite readers to book a consultation for their own matter.

Q: Wakeel ya law firm ki website mein kya likhna chahiye?
A: Website mein practice areas, wukla ki enrolment aur courts, daftar ka pata aur rabte ka tareeqa saaf likhein. Case jeetne ki guarantee ya behtareen hone ke daawe na karein. Website banane se pehle Pakistan Bar Council aur apni provincial bar council ke maujooda qawaid zaroor parh lein.

Key points:
- Parents visit a school website for admissions, fees, timings, notices and contact; make these one tap away.
- An online admission form saves queues, but collect only what you need and protect it.
- Publish fee schedules clearly, with what is included, to cut repeated phone calls.
- Never publish children's photos or names without written parental consent.
- Start with a strong website; add a parent portal when you are ready to keep its data updated daily.

Q: How much does a school website cost in Pakistan?
A: A small academy website of up to 5 pages starts from Rs 40,500, and a school website with admissions, fee schedules, notices and a gallery of up to 10 pages starts from Rs 85,500. A parent portal with attendance, results and fee status is a web application starting from Rs 360,000.

Q: Can parents apply for admission online?
A: Yes. A short online admission form can collect the child's details, class applied for and parent contact details, send the school a notification and give parents an automatic acknowledgement. Q: Should a school publish fees on its website?

Q: School ki website mein kya kya hona chahiye?

- Delivery marketplaces bring new customers but charge commission on each order; direct orders keep that margin.

- Delivery zones, minimum order and delivery charges must be set clearly per area.
- WhatsApp ordering from the menu suits many Pakistani restaurants better than a full checkout at first.
- You need your own riders or a delivery arrangement to take direct delivery orders.

Q: Can a restaurant take online orders without a delivery app?

Q: How much does a restaurant ordering website cost?

Q: How much commission do food delivery apps charge?

An agency site with a listings section starts from Rs 85,500; a portal with agent logins and lead routing is a web app from Rs 360,000.
Key points:
- Buyers and tenants judge a property website on whether listings are real, current and complete.
- A consistent listing structure, with price, size, location, photos and status, makes search and filters work.
- Area and society pages help your site appear for local searches and show genuine local knowledge.
- Route each enquiry to the listing's agent on WhatsApp, and track response times.
- Remove or mark sold and rented properties quickly; stale listings destroy trust.

Q: How much does a real estate website cost in Pakistan?

Q: What should a property listing include?
A: Every listing should state purpose, type, city, society and block, size in the units buyers expect, price or rent and advance, status, recent real photos and the agent's name and WhatsApp. Fixed fields matter because filters, search and area pages depend on consistent data entered the same way by every agent.

Q: Can I add my property listings to Google Maps?
A: Not as individual listings. Google's Business Profile help states that profiles are not for properties for rent or sale. You can create a profile for your agency office, with accurate address, hours and photos, and link it to the listings on your website so people searching locally find you.

Q: How do I stop old listings showing on my property website?
A: Give every listing a review date and expire it automatically unless an agent confirms it is still available. Require agents to mark properties sold or rented when deals close, and show the status clearly. Regular clean-ups keep the site trustworthy and reduce wasted calls.

Q: How should real estate leads be handled from a website?
A: Send each enquiry to the listing's agent on WhatsApp with the listing ID, copy a manager, and reassign the lead if the agent does not reply within a set time. Record source, listing, agent and outcome in a simple lead list, so you know which listings and channels bring deals.

Q: Property dealer ki website mein kya hona chahiye?
A: Har property ka sahi rate, size, society aur block, asli tasveerein aur agent ka WhatsApp number ho. Bik chuki ya kiraye par chali gayi property foran hata dein ya mark karein. Har society ka alag page banayein jismein asal maloomat ho, aur har enquiry par jaldi jawab dein.

## Export Company Website for Pakistani Exporters: Features That Win Foreign Buyers
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/exporter-website-b2b-pakistan
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: An export company website wins foreign buyers when it shows exactly what you make, your capacity and minimum order, real certifications, factory photos, a request-for-quotation form and contact hours in the buyer's time zone. Pakistan is 4 to 5 hours ahead of the UK. A 10-page exporter website starts from Rs 85,500.
Key points:
- Foreign buyers judge an exporter by product detail, capacity, compliance and how quickly you reply.
- A request-for-quotation form that asks the right questions turns visitors into qualified leads.
- Show only certifications and audits you genuinely hold, with certificate numbers buyers can verify.
- Write in clear international English, with units, Incoterms and lead times buyers expect.
- State your working hours in buyers' time zones and reply to enquiries within one business day.

Q: What should an exporter's website include?
A: It should include product category pages with specifications and real photos, monthly capacity, minimum order quantity and lead times, factory and quality process details, genuine certifications with numbers and validity, a request-for-quotation form with file upload, and contact details with working hours shown in buyers' time zones.

Q: How can a Pakistani exporter get foreign buyers through a website?
A: Create a page for each main product with specifications and photos so buyers searching for that product can find you, add a clear RFQ form, and reply to enquiries within one business day. Use the website alongside trade shows, B2B platforms and direct outreach, which send buyers to check your site.

Q: Should I display certifications on my export website?
A: Yes, but only those your factory genuinely holds, with the certificate number, issuing body and validity date, and a link to the issuer's verification page where available. Never show an expired certificate or a logo you are not entitled to use. Buyers check, and false claims end relationships.

Q: What is an RFQ form?
A: An RFQ, or request for quotation, form lets a buyer ask for your price on a specific order. It should capture company and country, product specification with an optional file upload, quantities, destination, preferred Incoterm, target date and whether samples are needed, so you can quote without several rounds of emails.

Q: What time difference should exporters show for UK buyers?
A: Pakistan is 4 hours ahead of the UK during British Summer Time and 5 hours ahead in winter, because Pakistan does not change its clocks. It is 1 hour ahead of the UAE all year. Show your office hours with these equivalents on the contact page.

Q: Exporter ki website mein kya hona chahiye?
A: Har product ka alag page jismein specifications aur asli tasveerein hon, monthly capacity aur MOQ, factory ki tasveerein, sirf asli certifications number ke saath, aur RFQ form. Rabte ke page par UK, Gulf aur US ke hisaab se office timings likhein aur har enquiry ka aik din mein jawab dein.

## B2B Catalogue Website for Manufacturers: Spec Sheets, Distributor Logins and Enquiry Routing
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/b2b-catalogue-website-manufacturers
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A B2B catalogue website gives dealers, distributors and contractors searchable product pages with specifications, downloadable spec sheets and catalogues, and an enquiry that reaches the right sales person. A public catalogue of up to 10 pages starts from Rs 85,500; a dealer portal with logins and price lists is a web app from Rs 360,000.
Key points:
- A B2B catalogue serves trade buyers who need specifications, model numbers and availability more than persuasion.
- Structured product data, such as model, size, material and rating, makes search and filters work.
- Keep downloadable catalogues and spec sheets current, with the version and date on each file.
- Dealer and distributor logins can show trade prices, stock and order history privately.
- Route enquiries by product line and region so the right sales person replies quickly.

Q: What does a trade catalogue site do for a manufacturer?
A: It is a manufacturer's searchable online product catalogue for trade buyers such as dealers, distributors and contractors. It shows model numbers, specifications, photos and downloadable spec sheets, and routes enquiries to the right sales person. Some include a private dealer portal with trade prices, stock and online reordering.

Q: How is a trade catalogue different from an online store?
A: An online store sells to consumers with public prices, a cart and payment. A B2B catalogue serves trade buyers who need specifications, quantities and trade pricing, so it usually ends in an enquiry, quotation or dealer reorder rather than an instant card payment. Trade prices often sit behind a dealer login.

Q: Do I need a dealer portal on my manufacturer website?
A: Only if you can keep it current. A portal with tiered price lists, stock, reorders and order history saves calls and errors, but needs someone to approve dealers and update prices and stock. If that is not possible yet, start with a public catalogue and good enquiry routing.

Q: How should I prepare products for a catalogue website?
A: Prepare one spreadsheet with every product's name, model number, category, key specifications, finishes, packing details, photos and spec sheet file. Use the same fields and units for every product. Consistent data is what makes search, filters and comparison work for trade buyers on the website.

Q: Should spec sheets require an email to download?
A: It depends on your goal. Open downloads reach more buyers and are easier for contractors in a hurry. Asking for an email gives you leads to follow up but discourages some visitors. Many manufacturers keep spec sheets open and gate only full catalogues or technical drawings.

Q: Manufacturer ki catalogue website mein kya hona chahiye?
A: Har product ka model number, size, material aur doosri specifications, tasveerein aur download hone wali spec sheet honi chahiye. Filters se dealer apni zaroorat ka model dhoond sake. Enquiry form product aur sheher ke hisaab se sahi salesman tak jaye, aur zaroorat ho to dealers ke liye login rakhein.

## Salon Booking Website for Salons and Spas: Service Menus, Deposits and Fewer No-Shows
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/salon-spa-booking-website
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A salon booking website shows your full service menu with prices and duration, lets clients pick a stylist and time, takes a deposit for long or bridal services, and sends a reminder 1 day before. A salon website with WhatsApp booking starts from Rs 40,500; live slot booking with deposits is a web app from Rs 360,000.
Key points:
- Clients want to see services, prices, duration and real work before they book.
- Booking by stylist and service length stops double bookings and idle chairs.
- Deposits for bridal and long services reduce costly no-shows.
- A reminder by WhatsApp or SMS the day before is the simplest way to cut missed appointments.
- Photos of clients' hair or makeup need their consent, especially for bridal work.

Q: Do salons need online booking?
A: Small salons often do well with a WhatsApp booking button and a clear service menu. Salons with several stylists benefit from live slot booking that blocks time by service length, prevents double bookings and shows each stylist's day. Make sure walk-ins and phone bookings go into the same calendar.

Q: How can a salon reduce no-shows?
A: Send a reminder the day before with a one-tap confirm or reschedule link, and a short second reminder before early or bridal bookings. Ask for a deposit on long and bridal services, with a clear cancellation policy shown before payment. Most no-shows are forgetfulness, so reminders help most.

Q: Should a salon take deposits online?
A: For bridal makeup, long hair treatments and spa packages, yes, because those slots are hard to refill. Take a fixed amount or a share of the price by wallet, Raast or bank transfer, and show your cancellation and refund policy before the client pays. Short services rarely need a deposit.

Q: How much does a salon booking website cost?
A: A salon website with service menu, gallery and WhatsApp booking starts from Rs 40,500, or Rs 85,500 for a fuller site. Live slot booking by stylist with deposits, reminders and a staff calendar is a web application starting from Rs 360,000. Hosting, a domain and any payment charges are extra.

Q: Can I post client photos on my salon website?
A: Only with the client's consent, and respect anyone who declines, especially brides and clients who value privacy. Crop faces where the result can still be shown, and use real, unedited photos. Heavy filters create expectations the salon cannot meet and can lead to unhappy clients later.

Q: Parlour ki website par booking kaise lein?
A: Website par har service ki qeemat aur waqt likhein aur WhatsApp booking button lagayen. Agar kai stylists hain to online slot booking behtar hai. Bridal aur lambi services ke liye advance lein aur cancellation policy pehle bata dein. Aik din pehle WhatsApp par reminder bhejne se no-shows kam hote hain.

## Gym Website in Pakistan: Membership Plans, Class Schedules, Payments and a Member Portal
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/gym-website-pakistan

Short answer: A gym website in Pakistan should show membership plans and prices clearly, a live class timetable, separate ladies' timings if you offer them, trainer profiles and a quick WhatsApp enquiry. Key points:
- Visitors compare membership plans and prices first; a clear plan table converts better than 'call for rates'.
- A class timetable with booking limits stops overcrowded classes and empty slots.
- Many Pakistani gyms run separate ladies' timings or sections; show them clearly.
- Automatic card renewals are not always available locally, so payment links and reminders often work better.
- A member portal is only worth building if your staff will keep attendance, plans and payments updated.

Q: Should a gym show membership prices on its website?
A: Yes. Many visitors compare gyms by price, and 'call for rates' sends them to competitors whose prices they can see. Show each plan's duration and price, admission fees separately, what is included and any freeze policy. If you run an offer, show the regular price and the offer end date.

Q: Can gym members pay monthly fees online in Pakistan?
A: Yes, through a payment link, wallet, card gateway, Raast or bank transfer. Automatic recurring card charges depend on your payment provider and members' cards, so check with your gateway first. Many gyms send a renewal reminder with a payment link and let members pay at the desk as well.

Q: Do gyms need a class booking system?
A: If your popular classes fill up or run half empty, booking with capacity limits and a waiting list helps. Members book a spot, cancel before a cut-off and free the place for others. Small gyms can start with WhatsApp class booking and move to a system when demand grows.

Q: What should a gym member portal include?
A: Plan and expiry dates, payment history and receipts, class bookings, attendance from QR or card check-in, and trainer notes. It only works if staff keep it updated. Check whether your existing gym management software already offers a member app that the website can link to before building one.

Q: Gym ki website mein kya hona chahiye?

## Pharmacy Website in Pakistan: Product Catalogue, Prescription Handling and WhatsApp Ordering
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/pharmacy-website-pakistan
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A pharmacy website in Pakistan should offer a searchable catalogue, WhatsApp ordering, prescription upload with pharmacist review for prescription-only items, and a clear privacy policy. Rules on selling medicines online can change, so confirm them with DRAP and your provincial authority first. A catalogue site starts from Rs 85,500; a full store from Rs 157,500.
Key points:
- Selling medicines is regulated; confirm current rules on online orders and delivery with DRAP and your provincial health authority.
- Separate general products, such as personal care, from prescription-only medicines in the catalogue and checkout.
- Prescription items should need an uploaded prescription and a pharmacist's check before dispatch.
- WhatsApp ordering suits many local pharmacies better than a full cart at first.
- Prescriptions and order histories are health data; collect little, protect it and limit access.

Q: Can a pharmacy sell medicines online in Pakistan?
A: Rules on online sale and delivery of medicines are set by DRAP and provincial authorities and can change. We are web developers, not regulatory advisers. Confirm the current position for your licence and products with DRAP, your provincial drug authority and your adviser before building an online ordering system.

Q: How should a pharmacy website handle prescription medicines?
A: Prescription-only items should only be ordered with an uploaded prescription, reviewed by a registered pharmacist for validity, dose and quantity before confirmation. The pharmacist contacts the customer if anything is unclear. Store prescriptions securely with the order and keep a record of who approved each one.

Q: Is WhatsApp ordering enough for a pharmacy?
A: For many local pharmacies, it is the best first step. A searchable catalogue with WhatsApp buttons and a 'send your prescription' option fits how customers already order. Staff confirm stock and price, the pharmacist checks prescription items, and a full checkout can follow when volume grows.

Q: How much does a pharmacy website cost?
A: A catalogue website with search, WhatsApp ordering, prescription chat and delivery information starts from Rs 85,500. A full online store with cart, prescription upload at checkout and pharmacist approval starts from Rs 157,500. Hosting, a domain and payment charges are extra, and scope depends on what your licence allows.

Q: How should a pharmacy protect customers' prescriptions?
A: Store prescriptions in a protected part of the system, not in email or shared folders. Limit access to the pharmacist and staff who need it, use HTTPS and two-step login, delete or archive old files under a written policy, and avoid sharing prescription images between staff phones or groups.

Q: Medical store ki website par dawaiyon ka order kaise lein?
A: Website par products ki list aur WhatsApp button lagayen, aur prescription bhejne ka aasan tareeqa dein. Prescription wali dawai sirf pharmacist ke check karne ke baad bhejein. Online dawai bechne ke maujooda qawaid DRAP aur apni provincial authority se pehle confirm kar lein.

## Travel Agency Website in Pakistan: Package Pages, Visa Information and Enquiries That Convert
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/travel-agency-website-pakistan

Key points:

- Present visa information as guidance only, and never imply official visa processing you are not licensed for.
- Enquiry forms should capture travel dates, number of travellers and package so staff can quote quickly.
- Take payments in stages with written terms, and state cancellation and refund rules before any payment.

Q: What should a travel agency website include?
A: It should include dated package pages with inclusions, exclusions, hotels, itinerary and per-person prices by room sharing, a visa guidance page presented as general information, genuine licence details, office address and map, package-specific enquiry forms or WhatsApp buttons, clear payment and cancellation terms and a privacy policy.

Q: Can a travel agency website offer visa services?
A: Only describe services you are licensed and authorised to provide, and describe them accurately, such as document preparation or appointment help. Never imply you issue visas or guarantee approval. Visa rules are set by destination countries and change often, so date your guidance and link to official sources.

Q: How should Umrah packages be shown on a website?
A: Show each departure on its own page with dates, nights in each city, hotel names or category and distance, inclusions, exclusions and per-person prices by quad, triple and double sharing, plus child prices. State your authorisation details exactly as issued, and remove packages after departure.

Q: How can travellers trust an online travel agency?
A: They look for things they can verify: registered business name, genuine licence numbers, a physical office address with map, landline numbers, named staff contacts and dated reviews. Written terms for payments, cancellations and refunds, accepted before the first payment, also build trust and prevent disputes later.

Q: How much does a travel agency website cost?

Q: Should a contractor show PEC registration on the website?
A: If your firm is registered, yes. The Pakistan Engineering Council states that only PEC-registered firms are authorised to undertake government and public sector engineering projects, so clients often check. Show the registration number, category and validity exactly as issued, and keep it updated when renewed.

Q: What is a capability statement for a construction company?
A: It is a short document, usually two to six pages, summarising your company, registrations, key projects, equipment, team, safety approach and contacts. Procurement and pre-qualification teams ask for it often. Keep a dated PDF on your website and update it yearly or after major projects.

Q: Can I show client names on my construction portfolio?

## NGO and Trust Website in Pakistan: Online Donations, Annual Reports and Donor Transparency
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/ngo-donation-website-pakistan
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: An NGO website in Pakistan should make giving easy through bank transfer, Raast, wallets and cards where available, publish annual reports and audited accounts, show where money goes, and protect donor details. A 10-page trust website with donation pages starts from Rs 85,500; a donor portal with receipts and recurring pledges is a web app from Rs 360,000.
Key points:
- Donors give when they trust you: show who you are, what you do, and where the money went.
- Offer the donation methods your donors use: bank transfer and Raast, wallets, cards where available, and international transfers.
- Separate donation types, such as Zakat, Sadaqah and general donations, if you accept more than one.
- Publish annual reports and audited accounts, and update programme results at least yearly.
- Donor names, amounts and contact details are private; publish them only with permission.

Q: How can an NGO in Pakistan accept donations online?
A: Show bank transfer details with IBAN and a Raast QR code, mobile wallet details, and a card option through a Pakistani payment gateway if your organisation qualifies. For overseas donors, show international transfer details with the SWIFT code. Ask donors to add a reference so you can match payments and send receipts.

Q: Can a Pakistani NGO use Stripe or PayPal for donations?
A: Stripe does not list Pakistan as a supported country, so a Pakistan-registered organisation cannot open a Stripe account, and PayPal does not offer Pakistan-based accounts for receiving payments. Use international bank transfers for overseas donors, and Pakistani gateways, wallets and Raast for local donors.

Q: What should an NGO publish to build donor trust?
A: Publish your legal name, registration number as issued and address, trustees or board members, programme pages with results, annual reports, audited financial statements and a spending breakdown. Date everything and keep it current. Donors trust organisations that show where money went, not just what they plan to do.

Q: Should Zakat be collected separately on a donation website?
A: If you accept Zakat alongside other donations, give it a separate option on the donation form or a separate account, and explain on the website how Zakat funds are used. Many donors want this clarity, and keeping the funds separate makes reporting easier for your organisation as well.

Q: How much does an NGO website cost?
A: A trust or NGO website with programme pages, a donate page, reports archive and contact page starts from Rs 85,500 for up to 10 pages, or Rs 40,500 for five. A donor portal with receipts, recurring pledges and programme reporting is a web application starting from Rs 360,000.

Q: NGO ki website par donation kaise lein?
A: Donate page par bank account ka IBAN, Raast QR code aur wallet ki tafseel dein, aur agar gateway ijazat de to card option bhi rakhein. Zakat aur Sadaqah ke alag option banayein. Saalana report aur audited accounts website par lagayen taake donors ko pata chale paisa kahan kharch hua.

## Hotel Website Booking Engine for Hotels and Guest Houses: Rooms, Rates and Direct Bookings
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/hotel-guest-house-booking-website
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A hotel website booking engine lets guests check availability and book rooms directly, so you keep the commission an online travel agency would charge. Small guest houses can start with an enquiry form and WhatsApp; hotels on several booking sites need a booking engine linked to a channel manager. Our booking builds start from Rs 360,000.
Key points:
- Booking sites bring guests who would not find you otherwise; they also charge commission on each booking.
- Direct bookings from your website suit repeat guests, corporate guests and people who found you on Google Maps.
- Every room type needs its own page with real photos, size, beds, view and what the rate includes.
- If you sell rooms on several sites, a channel manager keeps availability in step and prevents double bookings.
- Take a deposit or card guarantee for direct bookings, with a clear cancellation policy.

Q: What is a hotel booking engine?
A: It is software on your website that lets guests check room availability for their dates, see rates and book directly, usually with a deposit or card payment. Connected to a channel manager, it keeps availability in step with the booking sites where you also sell rooms, preventing double bookings.

Q: Do small guest houses need a booking engine?
A: Not always. A guest house with a few rooms and mostly direct guests can do well with room pages, an enquiry form and WhatsApp, with staff confirming each booking. A booking engine pays off when you sell on several booking sites or handle many bookings every week.

Q: How much commission do hotel booking sites charge?
A: Each booking site sets commission in its contract with you, and those terms are not published reliably. Look up the rate in your agreement and apply it to the value of bookings that could come direct, such as returning and corporate guests. Subtract gateway charges to see the real saving from direct bookings.

Q: What is a channel manager?
A: A channel manager is software that connects your room inventory to your website and every booking site. When a room sells on one, availability updates on all the others. It prevents double bookings and saves staff from closing rooms on each site by hand during busy periods.

Q: How much does a hotel booking website cost?
A: A guest house website with room pages, gallery, enquiry form and WhatsApp starts from Rs 85,500. A booking engine with live availability, deposits and confirmations, or a channel manager connection, is a web application starting from Rs 360,000, with the final price depending on integrations and the number of properties.

Q: Guest house ki website par direct booking kaise lein?
A: Har kamre ka alag page banayein jismein asli tasveerein, size, beds aur rate mein kya shaamil hai likha ho. Chhote guest house WhatsApp aur enquiry form se shuru kar sakte hain. Booking ke liye Raast ya wallet se advance lein aur cancellation policy pehle bata dein.

## Logistics Company Website: Shipment Tracking, Instant Quotes and Business Account Portals
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/logistics-company-website
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A logistics company website should let clients track shipments by number, request or calculate a quote, and log in to a business account for bookings, invoices and proof of delivery. Tracking and portals pull data from your operations system, so they are web applications, starting from Rs 360,000.
Key points:
- Clients judge a logistics company on visibility: where is my shipment, and when will it arrive?
- Tracking on the website depends on clean status data from your operations or warehouse system.
- An instant quote calculator works for standard services; complex freight needs a fast quote request form.
- A business account portal reduces calls by showing bookings, invoices and proof of delivery.
- Build in phases: public website and tracking first, then quotes, then the client portal.

Q: What should a logistics company website include?
A: It should include clear service and coverage pages, shipment tracking by number, a quote calculator for standard services or a quote request form for complex freight, and, for regular clients, a business account portal with bookings, invoices and proof of delivery. Contact details and response times should be easy to find.

Q: How does shipment tracking on a website work?
A: Each shipment gets a tracking number, and staff or drivers update its status at every step in your operations system. The website reads those updates through an API or database connection and shows the history to anyone who enters the number. Tracking is only accurate if status updates are timely.

Q: Should a freight company offer instant quotes online?
A: Only for standard services with clear rates, such as parcels by weight and zone or truckloads between fixed cities. Complex freight depends on cargo, volume, routing and customs, so a calculator can mislead. Use a detailed quote request form for those and reply within a stated time.

Q: What is a logistics client portal?
A: It is a private area where business clients log in to book shipments, see live status, download proof of delivery and view invoices and statements. Several staff from the client company can have their own logins. It reduces calls and emails and helps keep regular clients loyal.

Q: How much does a logistics website with tracking cost?
A: A public logistics website with services, coverage and a quote request form starts from Rs 85,500. Tracking, quote calculators and client portals connect to your operations data and are built as a web application starting from Rs 360,000, with the final price depending on the systems being connected.

Q: Logistics company ki website mein kya hona chahiye?
A: Services aur coverage ka saaf bayan, tracking number se shipment check karne ki sahulat, quote ka form ya standard services ke liye calculator, aur regular clients ke liye login jismein bookings, invoices aur delivery ka saboot ho. Tracking tab hi kaam karti hai jab status waqt par update ho.

## Clinic Website in Lahore: How Clinics in DHA, Johar Town and Model Town Get Found and Booked
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/clinic-website-lahore
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A clinic website in Lahore gets found when it works with a verified Google Business Profile, honest patient reviews and accurate details for your area, such as DHA, Johar Town or Model Town. It gets booked when the first screen shows doctor, timings, fees and a WhatsApp button. Clinic websites start from Rs 40,500.
Key points:
- Most local patients find a Lahore clinic through Google Maps results, so the Business Profile matters as much as the website.
- Name, address, phone and timings must match exactly on the website, the profile and every listing.
- Ask every patient for an honest review, but never offer rewards or ask only happy patients; Google's rules forbid both.
- Write an area page only for a branch or a real service area, never city-name copies.
- Being in Lahore, we can visit your clinic for photos and a walk-through of how patients book today.

Q: How can my clinic appear on Google Maps in Lahore?
A: Create and verify a Google Business Profile with your real clinic name, the most specific category, exact address with the pin on your entrance, accurate hours, a phone that is answered and real photos. Link it to your website, keep details identical everywhere and collect honest reviews from every patient.

Q: Can I offer patients a discount for a Google review?
A: No. Google's review policy does not allow reviews posted because of an incentive, including discounts or free services. It also forbids asking only happy patients. Ask every patient for an honest review with a direct link, and reply politely to all reviews without mentioning medical details.

Q: Should my clinic website have pages for different Lahore areas?
A: Only if you have a branch there or something genuinely different to say. Give each real branch its own page with doctors, timings, directions and photos. Copying the same page for many neighbourhoods with only the name changed adds nothing for patients and can harm how search engines see the website.

Q: Why do my clinic timings need to match everywhere?
A: Patients and search engines rely on consistent details. If your website, Google profile and Facebook page show different hours or numbers, patients may arrive when you are closed or call a number nobody answers, and search engines trust the listing less. Choose one format and use it everywhere.

Q: Can you visit our clinic in Lahore?
A: Yes. Our office is in Awan Town, Lahore, and we can visit clinics in the city to see how bookings work, arrange photos of the entrance and waiting area and set up the Google Business Profile with you as the owner. Projects follow a written scope and fixed price.

Q: Lahore mein clinic Google Maps par kaise aaye?
A: Google Business Profile banayein aur verify karein, clinic ka asli naam, sahi pata, timings aur chalta hua phone number dein, aur darwaze aur waiting area ki tasveerein lagayen. Har mareez se imaandari se review ka kahein, lekin review ke badle discount na dein. Website par yahi maloomat bilkul aik jaisi rakhein.

## How to Hire Pakistani Web Developers Safely: Costs, Risks, Contracts and Communication
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/hire-pakistani-web-developers
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: To hire Pakistani web developers safely, agree a written scope and fixed price, pay in milestones, keep the domain, hosting and code repository in your own name, and set a regular call inside the overlapping working hours. Our published prices start at Rs 40,500 for a 5-page website and Rs 360,000 for a web application, invoiced in rupees.
Key points:
- Pakistani developers can deliver good work at lower cost, but the savings only hold with clear scope and communication.
- The main risks are vague scope, poor communication, ownership disputes and payment problems; each has a simple safeguard.
- Keep the domain, hosting, code repository and admin accounts in your name from day one.
- Pay against milestones with written acceptance criteria, never the full amount upfront.
- Overlap with the UK and Gulf is good; with North America it is short, so plan a fixed daily or weekly call.

Q: Is it safe to hire web developers from Pakistan?
A: It can be, with the same safeguards you would use anywhere: a written scope and fixed price, milestone payments tied to accepted work, accounts and code in your name, a staging site for testing and a regular call. Most problems come from vague scope and poor communication, not from location.

Q: How much do Pakistani web developers charge?
A: Prices vary widely between freelancers and established firms. Our published prices start at Rs 22,500 for a landing page, Rs 40,500 for a 5-page website and Rs 157,500 for an online store, with web applications within Rs 360,000 to Rs 1,350,000. We invoice in Pakistani rupees, converted at the rate on the payment date.

Q: How do I protect my intellectual property when outsourcing to Pakistan?
A: Sign a written agreement that transfers ownership of code, design and content to you after final payment, includes confidentiality terms, and requires the code to be kept in a repository you control. Keep domains, hosting and admin accounts in your name throughout, and take legal advice for complex projects.

Q: What time difference is there between Pakistan and the UK?
A: Pakistan uses UTC+5 all year without daylight saving. When UK clocks go forward the gap is four hours; in winter it is five. That usually gives four to five hours of overlap during the UK morning, which suits a daily or weekly call.

Q: How do I pay a developer in Pakistan?
A: The most common method is an international bank transfer to the developer's or company's Pakistani bank account, in milestones. Some clients use money transfer services such as Wise, or invoicing platforms such as Payoneer. We invoice in rupees and take payment by international bank transfer.

Q: Should I hire a freelancer or a company in Pakistan?
A: A freelancer can suit a small, well-defined task at low cost. A company is safer for larger or longer projects because work continues if one person leaves, there is review and testing, and you have a registered business to deal with. Check live work and references either way.

Q: Can Pakistani developers work in my time zone?
A: Partly. Overlap with the UK and Gulf is good within normal Pakistani hours. For North America, overlap is short or nil, so teams agree a fixed call time, sometimes late evening in Pakistan or early morning in North America, and rely on written updates and shared task boards between calls.

Q: Do Pakistani developers sign NDAs?
A: Reputable firms do. A non-disclosure agreement protects your business information, designs and plans. For agencies reselling work, white-label terms also prevent the developer from contacting your clients or showing the work in their portfolio. Ask for these terms before sharing confidential material.

## White Label Web Development: How Agencies Work With a Pakistani Team Under Their Own Brand
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/white-label-web-development-pakistan
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: White label web development means a partner team builds websites that your agency delivers under its own brand. With a Pakistani team, agencies typically sign an NDA, agree branding rules, run work through a staging site and QA checklist, and hold 1 or 2 calls a week. Our projects start from Rs 40,500 per website.
Key points:
- In white label work, the partner team stays invisible to your client; your agency owns the relationship and the brand.
- An NDA and written white-label terms come first: no contact with your clients, no portfolio use, no credits.
- A clear workflow, from brief to staging to handover, prevents the agency becoming a message relay.
- Quality assurance before your client sees anything protects your reputation.
- Start with one or two projects to test fit before moving larger volumes.

Q: What is white label web development?
A: It is an arrangement where a partner team builds websites that an agency sells and delivers under its own brand. The agency's client sees only the agency. The partner handles design or development behind the scenes, while the agency keeps the client relationship, pricing and branding.

Q: How do I stop a white label partner contacting my clients?
A: Agree written terms before sharing any client material: a non-disclosure agreement, a no-client-contact rule, a non-solicitation clause and no footer credits or portfolio use. Keep domains and hosting in your or your client's name, and route all client communication through your agency.

Q: How does quality control work with an offshore white label team?
A: Agree a written QA checklist covering mobile layout, speed, forms, links, browsers, accessibility basics and security settings. The partner completes it before each delivery, and the agency reviews work on a staging site before the client sees it. Review early projects closely, then sample-check.

Q: How should white label web development be priced?
A: Usually per project from a written scope and fixed price, so the agency knows its cost before quoting the client. Agencies with steady volume sometimes prefer a monthly dedicated developer. Published rupee prices from the partner make it easier to plan margins in your own currency.

Q: What time overlap is there for UK agencies working with Lahore?
A: Lahore sits four hours ahead of London from late March to late October and five hours ahead for the rest of the year, because Pakistan keeps one time all year. That leaves several hours of overlap during the UK morning, enough for one or two weekly calls and same-day replies to most questions.

Q: Can a white label partner put a credit link on websites?
A: Only with the agency's written permission. Under normal white-label terms, the partner adds no footer credits, hidden links or author tags, and does not show the work in its portfolio. Check the finished site's code and footer before launch to be sure.

## Dedicated Developer Model vs Fixed-Price Project: Which Suits Your Agency or Business?
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/dedicated-developer-vs-fixed-project
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: In the dedicated developer model, you pay a monthly fee for a developer who works on your priorities, which suits steady, changing work. A fixed-price project suits a defined website or app with clear scope. Agencies with 3 or more ongoing builds often benefit from a dedicated developer; one-off projects usually do not.
Key points:
- A dedicated developer is paid monthly and works on your list of tasks, which can change week to week.
- A fixed project has an agreed scope, timeline and price; changes go through change requests.
- Dedicated developers need management: someone must set priorities, review work and answer questions.
- Fixed projects transfer delivery risk to the supplier; dedicated models keep it with you.
- Start with a fixed project to build trust, then move to a dedicated arrangement if work is steady.

Q: What is a dedicated developer?
A: A dedicated developer works only or mainly on your tasks for a monthly fee. You set priorities each week and the developer works through them. It suits ongoing work with changing priorities, such as an agency's steady flow of client sites or a startup improving its product after launch.

Q: Is a dedicated developer cheaper than a fixed-price project?
A: Not automatically. A dedicated developer costs a known amount per month, but the total depends on how long you need them and how well you manage the work. Compare cost per delivered outcome over a few months, including your own management time, against fixed quotes for the same output.

Q: Who manages a dedicated offshore developer?
A: You do, or someone on your team. They keep a prioritised task list, answer questions quickly in the overlapping hours, review and test work regularly and hold a weekly planning call. Without that management, a dedicated arrangement drifts, and a fixed project usually gives better value.

Q: When is a fixed-price project the better choice?
A: When the work is defined and one-off, such as a new website, an online store or the first version of an app. You know the budget upfront, the supplier carries most of the delivery risk, and changes are handled through written change requests with agreed prices.

Q: Can I switch from a fixed project to a dedicated developer?
A: Yes. Many clients start with a fixed project to test communication and quality, then move to a dedicated developer if work becomes steady. The developer already knows your standards and code, which shortens the start-up time. You can move back to fixed projects if volume drops.

Q: How many projects justify a dedicated developer for an agency?
A: There is no fixed number, but agencies with several builds or ongoing client changes every month often find a dedicated developer worthwhile, because one person learns their standards. If work arrives occasionally or in unpredictable bursts, fixed projects and a maintenance plan are usually more economical.

## Offshore Team Time Zone Guide: Working Hours Overlap Between Lahore and the UK, US and Gulf
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/offshore-team-time-zones-lahore
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: For an offshore team time zone plan with Lahore, remember Pakistan is UTC+5 all year with no daylight saving. That gives about 4 to 5 hours of overlap with the UK, almost a full day with the UAE and Saudi Arabia, and little or none with North America, where a fixed early-morning or evening call is needed.
Key points:
- Pakistan Standard Time is UTC+5 all year; the gap changes only when your own country changes its clocks.
- The UK morning overlaps with the Lahore afternoon: about 5 hours in summer and 4 in winter.
- The UAE is 1 hour behind Pakistan and Saudi Arabia 2, so overlap covers most of the working day.
- US East and West have little or no overlap with normal Lahore hours, so plan one fixed call and work asynchronously.
- Working weeks differ too: Lahore works Monday to Saturday, while Gulf and Western weekends vary.

Q: What time zone is Lahore in?
A: Lahore, like the rest of Pakistan, uses Pakistan Standard Time, UTC+5, all year. Pakistan does not use daylight saving time, so the difference with your city changes only when your own country changes its clocks, as the UK, US and Canada do in spring and autumn.

Q: What is the time difference between Pakistan and the UK?
A: The difference is four hours while Britain is on summer time and five hours in winter. A Lahore working day of 9 AM to 6 PM therefore runs from 5 AM to 2 PM UK time in summer and 4 AM to 1 PM in winter, overlapping the UK morning.

Q: Can a Lahore team work with clients in the United States?
A: Yes, but there is little or no overlap within normal hours. Teams agree a fixed call at the edge of both days, such as early morning in New York and early evening in Lahore, and rely on written updates and a shared task board. Work progresses overnight from the client's view.

Q: How many hours overlap between Pakistan and the UAE?
A: Pakistan is 1 hour ahead of the UAE all year, so a 9 AM to 6 PM Lahore day runs from 8 AM to 5 PM UAE time. That gives about eight hours of overlap on shared working days, enough for calls and same-day replies.

Q: Do Pakistani offices work on Saturday?
A: Many do. Our office works Monday to Saturday, 9 AM to 6 PM, with shorter hours on Friday until 12:30 PM. Saturday work in Lahore can be useful for Western clients, because tasks can be finished before their Monday, while Saudi clients share Monday to Thursday as full days.

Q: How do you manage communication with an offshore team in a different time zone?
A: Write tasks with acceptance criteria and examples, batch questions at the start or end of your day, use one shared task board, record short screen videos for feedback and hold a fixed weekly call in the overlap window. A daily written update keeps everyone aligned without long meetings.

## Outsourcing Contract IP Ownership: NDAs, Code Rights and Clauses Explained in Plain English
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/outsourcing-website-ip-nda-code-ownership
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: In an outsourcing contract, IP ownership should be settled in writing before work starts: an NDA for confidentiality, an assignment clause transferring code and design to you after final payment, and a list of third-party and open-source parts you only license. Keep the repository, domain and hosting in your name from day 1. This is not legal advice.
Key points:
- Copyright in code and design generally starts with whoever creates it, so ownership must be transferred in writing.
- An NDA protects confidential information; it does not by itself transfer ownership of the work.
- An assignment clause transfers rights in the custom work, usually on final payment.
- Themes, plugins, libraries and fonts are licensed, not owned; the contract should list them.
- Control of the repository, domain and hosting matters as much as the words in the contract.

Q: Who owns the code when I outsource website development?
A: It depends on the contract. Copyright generally starts with whoever creates the work, so unless an agreement transfers the rights, the developer may keep them. A clear assignment clause, usually effective on final payment, transfers ownership of the custom code and design to you. Take legal advice for your country.

Q: Does an NDA give me ownership of the code?
A: Usually not. A non-disclosure agreement keeps your confidential information private, but it does not normally transfer ownership of the work. You need a separate assignment or ownership clause in the main development contract, as well as an NDA covering the information you share.

Q: What is an IP assignment clause?
A: It is a contract clause by which the developer transfers their rights in the custom work, such as code, designs and content, to the client, often once the final payment is made. It should be clear about which deliverables are covered and which third-party or pre-existing parts are only licensed.

Q: Can a developer reuse code from my project?
A: Developers often reuse their own general tools and techniques across projects, which is normal. Your contract should give you a licence to any such pre-existing tools used in your project, assign the custom work to you, and stop the developer reusing your confidential business logic or designs elsewhere.

Q: How do open-source licences affect ownership of my website?
A: Open-source parts such as WordPress, libraries and plugins stay under their own licences; you use them, but you do not own them. Some licences require keeping notices or sharing changes in certain cases. Ask your developer for a list of components and licences at handover.

Q: How can I protect my IP when outsourcing to another country?
A: Sign an NDA before sharing sensitive material, include an assignment clause in the main contract, list third-party components, and keep the code repository, domain, hosting and admin accounts in your own name from day one. Pay in milestones tied to delivered code, and take legal advice in your jurisdiction.

## How to Pay a Developer in Pakistan From Abroad: Bank Wire, Wise and Payoneer Compared
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/pay-web-developer-in-pakistan
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: To pay a developer in Pakistan, most overseas clients use an international bank transfer to the company's Pakistani bank account, against a rupee invoice and in milestones such as 30% to 40% upfront. Transfer services such as Wise, or Payoneer for freelancers, are alternatives. Our websites start from Rs 40,500, invoiced in rupees.
Key points:
- An international bank wire to the developer's business account is the standard method for agencies and companies.
- Transfer services such as Wise can cost less, where they support your country and Pakistan.
- Payoneer is common for freelancers and marketplace earnings; it collects payments from clients in many countries.
- A rupee invoice means the developer receives the agreed amount; you pay the equivalent in your currency on the day.
- Pay in milestones tied to delivered work, and verify bank details by phone before the first transfer.

Q: What is the best way to pay a developer in Pakistan?
A: For a company, an international bank transfer to its Pakistani business account against a written invoice is the most common and gives clear records. Transfer services such as Wise can cost less where available, and freelancers often use Payoneer. Check fees and availability on the day you pay.

Q: Can I use Wise to pay someone in Pakistan?
A: Wise is an international money transfer service, and availability depends on the country you send from and the receiving side. Check Wise's own site for whether it supports your route to a Pakistani bank account, the current fee and the delivery time before arranging a payment.

Q: Why do Pakistani agencies invoice in rupees?
A: A rupee invoice fixes the price in the developer's own currency, so they receive the agreed amount. You pay the equivalent in your currency at the rate on the payment day. It avoids disputes about exchange rates and keeps quotes comparable across projects.

Q: How much should I pay upfront to a developer?
A: A deposit of about 30% to 40% after the written scope is approved is common, followed by a mid-project payment after design approval or a working staging site, and the balance on delivery. Avoid paying the full amount upfront, and tie each payment to work you can see.

Q: How do I avoid sending money to the wrong account?
A: Confirm bank details by phone or video with a person you know before the first payment, and never accept changed details by email alone. Check the account title matches the company or person you contracted, and keep invoices and transfer receipts for every payment.

Q: Can I pay a Pakistani developer through PayPal?
A: Pakistan-based businesses generally cannot receive payments through PayPal, so most Pakistani developers and agencies ask for a bank transfer, a transfer service or Payoneer instead. Ask the developer which method they accept, and confirm the details directly with them before paying.

## Arabic Website Development for Gulf Businesses: Right-to-Left Layout, Fonts and SEO Done Right
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/arabic-rtl-website-development
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: Arabic website development means more than translating text: the layout must flip right to left, set with the HTML dir attribute as W3C advises, use Arabic fonts that render well on phones, and link English and Arabic pages with hreflang. A bilingual 10-page business website with us starts from Rs 85,500 plus translation.
Key points:
- Arabic is written right to left, so menus, layouts, icons and forms must mirror, not just the text.
- W3C advises setting direction with the dir attribute in HTML rather than with CSS alone.
- Bilingual sites should give each language its own URLs and connect them with hreflang annotations.
- Choose Arabic web fonts designed for screens, and test them on real phones.
- Use a professional Arabic translator for customer-facing text; machine translation alone reads poorly to native speakers.

Q: What is an RTL website?
A: An RTL, or right-to-left, website displays languages such as Arabic and Urdu that read from right to left. The whole layout mirrors: navigation starts on the right, columns swap sides and directional icons flip. The HTML dir attribute tells browsers to display the page right to left.

Q: Is translating my English website into Arabic enough?
A: No. Besides translation, the layout must flip right to left, directional icons must mirror, forms must align correctly, Arabic fonts must render well and each language needs its own URLs with hreflang links. Without these, an Arabic site feels broken to native readers even if the words are right.

Q: How should a bilingual Arabic and English website be set up for Google?
A: Give each language its own URLs, such as /en/ and /ar/, connect equivalent pages with hreflang annotations, and add a visible language switcher. Google's multilingual guidance advises against automatically redirecting visitors by location. Check the set-up in Google Search Console after launch.

Q: How much does an Arabic website cost?
A: A bilingual Arabic and English business website of up to 10 pages starts from Rs 85,500 with us, with professional translation quoted separately or supplied by you. Online stores in both languages start from Rs 157,500. Prices are invoiced in Pakistani rupees and paid in milestones.

Q: Should I use machine translation for my Arabic website?
A: Use it for drafts at most. Machine translation often reads awkwardly to native speakers and can get tone and terminology wrong, which hurts a brand. Use a professional Arabic translator for customer-facing pages and have a native speaker on your team review everything before launch.

Q: Which numbers should an Arabic website use?
A: Decide between Western digits and Arabic-Indic digits and use your choice consistently across prices, phone numbers and dates. Many Gulf businesses use Western digits on websites, but follow your brand and audience. Whatever you choose, test that mixed numbers and Arabic text display in the correct order.

## Web Design for UK Small Business With an Offshore Team: Quality, GDPR and Cookies Covered

Our 5-page website starts from Rs 40,500, invoiced in rupees, with about 4 to 5 hours of overlap with UK mornings.
Key points:
- An offshore team can build a UK small business website well, but UK legal basics must be in the brief.
- The ICO publishes UK GDPR guidance; your website needs a privacy notice and careful handling of form data.
- Under PECR, non-essential cookies such as analytics and advertising need consent before they are set.
- Accessibility to WCAG standards helps customers and reduces risk.
- Keep the domain, hosting and accounts in your name, and review everything on a staging site.

Q: Can an offshore team build a UK small business website?
A: Yes, if the brief covers UK requirements such as a privacy notice under UK GDPR, cookie consent under PECR, accessibility and British English, and you review the work on a staging site. Keep the domain and accounts in your name, and agree a fixed price with milestone payments.

Q: Does my UK small business website need a cookie banner?
A: If it uses non-essential cookies, such as analytics or advertising, yes. The ICO's guidance says you must tell users about them and get consent, through a clear positive action, before setting them. Cookies strictly necessary for a service the user requested, such as a basket, are exempt.

Q: What does UK GDPR require from a small business website?
A: In practice, a clear privacy notice, forms that collect only what you need, secure handling and storage of submissions, a lawful basis for marketing emails and agreements with services that process data for you. Check the ICO's guidance and take advice for your specific business.

Q: What time overlap is there between the UK and Pakistan?
A: Pakistan keeps UTC+5 all year. Its working day overlaps the UK morning by about five hours during British Summer Time and four in winter, which is enough for design reviews and weekly calls. Most questions get answered the same UK working day.

Q: Should my UK website meet accessibility standards?
A: Building to the W3C's Web Content Accessibility Guidelines is good practice: it helps customers with disabilities, improves usability for everyone and reduces risk. Ask for logical headings, alt text, good contrast, labelled form fields and keyboard navigation, and test the site before launch.

Key points:
- Ontario's AODA requires public websites of organisations with 50 or more employees, and designated public sector bodies, to meet WCAG 2.0 Level AA.
- Smaller businesses are not covered by that rule but benefit from building accessibly anyway.
- If you serve French-speaking customers, especially in Quebec, check language requirements with an adviser.
- Pakistan is 9 to 13 hours ahead of Canada's main business centres, so plan fixed calls and written updates.
- Keep the domain, hosting and accounts in your name, and test on a staging site.

Q: Does my Canadian small business website need to follow the AODA?
A: The AODA website rule applies in Ontario to designated public sector organisations and to businesses or non-profits with 50 or more employees. They must make public websites meet WCAG 2.0 Level AA. Smaller businesses are not covered by that rule but benefit from accessible design. Other provinces have their own laws.

Q: What WCAG level does Ontario require for websites?
A: According to the Government of Ontario, public websites and web content published after 1 January 2012 must meet WCAG 2.0 Level AA, except success criteria 1.2.4 for live captions and 1.2.5 for pre-recorded audio descriptions. The requirement has applied since 1 January 2021 for covered organisations.

Q: Does my website need to be in French?

Q: How much does an offshore website cost for a Canadian business?

Q: How do I check an offshore developer understands accessibility?
