## Choosing an MVP Development Company: Scope Cuts, Realistic Cost and a 6-Week Build Plan
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/mvp-development-startups
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A good MVP development company helps you cut scope to the one workflow that proves your idea, then builds it in about 6 weeks with weekly demos. Our MVPs are web applications starting from Rs 360,000, with most first versions at the lower end of Rs 360,000 to Rs 1,350,000 when scope is kept tight.
Key points:
- An MVP exists to learn whether customers want your product, with the least effort, not to launch every feature.
- Cut scope to one user type and one core workflow; everything else waits for evidence.
- Write features as user stories with acceptance criteria, so the team builds the right thing.
- A six-week plan with weekly demos keeps decisions fast and surprises small.
- Own the code repository, cloud accounts and domain from day one.

Q: What is an MVP in software development?
A: A minimum viable product is the version of a product that lets a team learn the most about whether customers want it, with the least effort. For a web startup, that usually means one type of user completing one core task end to end, with basic admin handled manually.

Q: How much does MVP development cost?
A: Our MVPs are web applications starting from Rs 360,000. A tight MVP with one core workflow sits at the lower end of our Rs 360,000 to Rs 1,350,000 range, while payments, several user roles or integrations move it higher. Every project is quoted as a fixed price after a written scope.

Q: Can an MVP be built in six weeks?
A: Often, if scope is cut to one user type and one core workflow. A typical plan covers scope and set-up in week one, core features in weeks two to four, polish and testing in week five, and launch in week six, with a demo every week to keep decisions quick.

Q: Should my MVP be a mobile app or a web app?
A: For most startups, a responsive web app or progressive web app is the better first step, because one build reaches iPhone, Android and desktop users and updates instantly. Build native apps later if you need deep phone features or users clearly prefer an app.

Q: What should I ask an MVP development company?
A: Ask whether they will challenge your scope, show working software weekly, keep the code repository and cloud accounts in your name, write tests for the core flow, document the set-up, and continue or hand over cleanly after launch. Ask to see a live product they built.

Q: What happens after the MVP launches?
A: Measure what users do, talk to them and decide the next features based on evidence rather than the original wish list. Many startups keep the same team on a monthly arrangement to iterate, while others switch to fixed-price phases for each new set of features.

## How to Get Your Business Website on Google: A Practical Pakistan Guide With a 30-Day Plan
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/get-business-website-on-google
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: To get your website on Google, do 4 things: let Google index it through Search Console and a sitemap, create a verified Google Business Profile, publish pages that answer customers' questions, and earn genuine reviews and links. Indexing can take days to weeks; ranking takes longer, and no one can promise a position.
Key points:
- Getting on Google has two parts: being indexed, so Google knows your pages exist, and ranking, so they appear for useful searches.
- Google Search Console is free and shows whether your pages are indexed and which searches bring visitors.
- For local businesses, a verified Google Business Profile often brings more customers than the website alone.
- Pages that answer real customer questions in plain language are what rank over time.
- Expect indexing in days to weeks and real results in months; anyone guaranteeing a position is not being honest.

Q: How long does it take for a new website to appear on Google?
A: Google says crawling and indexing can take from a few days to a few weeks after you submit a sitemap or request indexing, and it does not promise that every page will be indexed. Ranking well for useful searches usually takes months and depends on content, competition and trust.

Q: Why is my website not showing on Google?
A: Common reasons are that Google has not indexed it yet, pages are set to noindex or blocked in robots.txt after development, the site is new with no links, or it is indexed but ranks too low to see. Check in Google Search Console, which shows the exact status of each page.

Q: Is it free to put my business on Google?
A: Yes. Indexing in Google Search, Google Search Console and Google Business Profile are all free. You pay only if you choose Google Ads or hire someone to build or improve your website. Be wary of anyone charging a fee simply to 'submit' your site to Google.

Q: Do I need a sitemap for my small business website?
A: Google says small, well-linked sites of about 500 pages or fewer may manage without one. Sitemaps still help new sites with few external links, and most website platforms create one automatically. Submitting it in Search Console is quick and lets you see any indexing problems.

Q: What is Google Search Console?
A: It is a free Google tool that shows whether your pages are indexed, which searches show your site, how many people click, which sites link to you and any problems Google finds, such as errors, security issues or penalties. Every business website should have it set up in the owner's name.

Q: Can anyone guarantee my website will be first on Google?
A: No. Google's own guide says there is no guarantee a site will be indexed and no shortcut to the top of results. Anyone promising a fixed position is either misleading you or using tactics that can get a site penalised. Good content, speed, reviews and genuine links improve your chances.

Q: Google par apna business kaise laayen?
A: Pehle Google Search Console mein apni website verify karein aur sitemap submit karein. Phir Google Business Profile banayein aur verify karein, asli tasveerein aur timings dein. Customers ke sawalon ke jawab wale pages likhein aur har customer se imaandari se review ka kahein. Natije hafton se mahinon mein aate hain.

Q: Does Google Business Profile help my website rank?
A: It mainly controls how your business appears on Google Maps and in local results, which for many local searches show above ordinary website results. Linking the profile to your website, keeping details consistent and collecting genuine reviews help customers find both the profile and the website.

Q: Should I use the meta keywords tag?
A: No. Google's SEO starter guide says Google Search does not use the keywords meta tag. Spend the effort instead on clear, unique page titles, helpful content that answers customer questions, fast mobile pages and descriptive headings, which all help both visitors and search engines.

## Google Business Profile in Pakistan: Setup, Verification and Fixing Common Local Problems
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/google-business-profile-pakistan
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A Google Business Profile in Pakistan is free and controls how your shop, clinic or office appears on Google Maps and Search. Sign in, add or claim the business, verify it by the method Google offers, such as a phone code or video, then add hours, photos and your website. Google says review usually takes up to 5 business days.
Key points:
- Business Profiles are for businesses that meet customers in person, at a location or in a service area, not online-only shops.
- Google chooses which verification methods you can use, such as phone or text, email, video or postcard.
- Write Pakistani addresses in one consistent format with block, sector or phase, and put the map pin on your entrance.
- Use a phone number that is answered during your listed hours.
- Keep yourself as owner and add staff or your developer as managers.

Q: Is Google Business Profile free in Pakistan?
A: Yes. Creating and managing a Google Business Profile is free. It controls how your business appears on Google Maps and Search. Google's help pages say profiles are for businesses that meet customers in person, at a location or in a service area; online-only businesses are not eligible.

Q: How do I verify my business on Google Maps in Pakistan?
A: After adding or claiming your business, choose from the verification options Google offers, which may include a phone or text code, email, a live video call or a postcard. Google recommends video where available. Review usually takes up to five business days, and you should never share your code.

Q: How should I write my Pakistani address on Google?
A: Choose one format and use it everywhere, for example shop or house number, street, block, sector or phase, area and city, with a nearby landmark in the description if helpful. Drag the map pin to your actual entrance. Consistent details help customers and Google trust your listing.

Q: Someone else controls my Google listing. What can I do?
A: Request ownership through Google Business Profile; Google contacts the current owner and may let you verify if they do not respond. In future, keep yourself as the primary owner and add staff, agencies or developers as managers, so you can remove them when they leave.

Q: Can I offer a discount for Google reviews?
A: No. Google's review policy does not allow reviews posted because of an incentive, such as discounts or free services, and forbids asking only happy customers. Ask every customer for an honest review, reply politely to all reviews, and do not let staff or family review your business.

Q: Google Maps par apni dukan kaise dalein?
A: Apne Google account se Google Business Profile kholen, dukan ka naam, category, pata aur phone number daalein, aur Google jo tareeqa de, jaise phone code ya video, us se verify karein. Map ka pin apne darwaze par rakhein, timings aur asli tasveerein lagayen, aur website ka link dein.

## SEO Friendly Website Development: The 15 Things That Should Be Built In Before Launch
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/seo-ready-website-checklist
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: SEO friendly website development means building in 15 basics before launch: indexable pages, a sitemap, Search Console, clean URLs, unique titles, one H1 per page, fast mobile pages, image alt text, internal links, HTTPS, structured data, redirects and analytics. These are included in our websites from Rs 40,500.
Key points:
- Technical basics decide whether Google can read your site at all; content decides whether it ranks.
- Most SEO problems on new sites are simple: pages left on noindex, missing titles, slow images or broken links.
- Every page needs a unique, descriptive title and one clear main heading.
- Structured data describes your business details for search engines in a standard format.
- Ask for this checklist in writing before you hire a developer, and check it at launch.

Q: What makes a website SEO friendly?
A: An SEO friendly website lets search engines find, read and understand every important page: indexable pages, a sitemap, clean URLs, unique titles and descriptions, logical headings, fast mobile pages, image alt text, internal links, HTTPS, structured data and redirects. Content quality then decides how well pages rank.

Q: Does an SEO friendly website guarantee rankings?
A: No. It removes technical obstacles, but rankings depend on how helpful your content is, competition for the search, and signals of trust such as reviews and genuine links. Google's own SEO guide says there are no shortcuts to the top of results.

Q: What is structured data on a website?
A: Structured data is code that labels facts on a page, such as your business name, address, phone, hours and location, in a standard format search engines read reliably. Visitors do not see it. It helps search engines understand your details and can make pages eligible for richer results.

Q: Should I use meta keywords for SEO?
A: There is no need. Google states plainly that its search does not read the meta keywords tag at all. Put the effort into unique, descriptive titles, helpful content that answers customer questions, clear headings, fast pages and internal links, which help both visitors and search engines understand your site.

Q: How do I check if my new website is SEO ready?
A: A week after launch, search site:yourdomain to see indexed pages, review Search Console's indexing report, test key pages with PageSpeed Insights or Lighthouse on mobile, check structured data with the Rich Results Test and click every menu link on a phone. Fix any errors found.

Q: SEO friendly website kaise banayein?
A: Website ke har page ka alag aur saaf title ho, aik main heading ho, tasveerein halki hon aur alt text ho, pages mobile par jaldi khulen, sitemap aur Search Console set ho, HTTPS ho aur purane pages ke redirects lagay hon. Developer se yeh 15 cheezein likhwa kar lein aur launch par check karein.

## AI Search Visibility for Business: Getting Mentioned by ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/ai-search-visibility-for-business
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: AI search visibility for business starts with ordinary good SEO. Google says AI Overviews and AI Mode have no extra technical requirements: pages must be indexed and eligible for a snippet. Beyond that, keep business details identical everywhere, publish clear, quotable facts, and earn mentions on trusted sites. No one can promise 1 AI mention.
Key points:
- Google says there are no additional technical requirements for AI Overviews and AI Mode beyond normal Search eligibility.
- Google also says you do not need special machine-readable files, markup or schema for these features.
- Consistent business details across your website, Business Profile and directories help AI systems identify you correctly.
- Clear, factual, well-structured answers are easier for both search engines and AI assistants to use.
- No one can guarantee that an AI assistant will mention your business; be wary of anyone who promises it.

Q: How can my business appear in Google AI Overviews?
A: Google says there are no extra technical requirements: your page must be indexed and eligible to show with a snippet. Follow normal SEO practice, keep important content in text, link pages internally, match structured data to visible text and keep your Business Profile current. Appearance is never guaranteed.

Q: Do I need an llms.txt file for AI search?
A: For Google's AI features, no: Google says you do not need new machine-readable files or special markup. llms.txt is a proposed file, not an official standard, and other AI providers may treat it differently. Adding one is harmless, but clear pages and consistent facts matter far more.

Q: Can someone guarantee ChatGPT will recommend my business?
A: No. AI assistants decide what to mention based on many sources and change over time. Anyone promising guaranteed mentions is overselling. What you can do is publish clear, factual pages, keep your details consistent everywhere and earn genuine reviews and mentions on trusted sites.

Q: What is generative engine optimisation?
A: It is a name for making content easy for AI systems to find, understand and quote. In practice, it overlaps heavily with good SEO: indexable pages, clear structure, factual and dated information, consistent business details, matching structured data and genuine mentions on reputable websites.

Q: Why do consistent business details matter for AI search?
A: AI systems combine information from your website, Business Profile, social pages and directories. If your name, address, phone or hours differ between them, it is harder to identify your business confidently. Using the exact same details everywhere makes it easier for search engines and AI tools to connect them.

Q: Can I stop Google's AI features from using my content?
A: Google points to controls such as nosnippet, data-nosnippet, max-snippet and noindex to limit how content appears in its AI features, and to Google-Extended for some other Google AI systems. These can also reduce how your pages appear in normal Search, so weigh the trade-off before using them.

## Schema Markup for Business Websites Explained Simply: Which Types Matter and How to Check Them
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/schema-markup-business-websites
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: Schema markup for business websites is hidden code that labels facts, such as your name, address, hours, products and FAQs, in the schema.org vocabulary so search engines read them reliably. Most businesses need 4 or 5 types: Organization or LocalBusiness, BreadcrumbList, and FAQPage or Product where relevant. Test it with Google's Rich Results Test.
Key points:
- Schema markup labels facts on a page in a standard vocabulary, schema.org, without changing what visitors see.
- LocalBusiness, or a more specific subtype, is the most useful type for businesses customers visit.
- Markup must match what is visible on the page; hidden or false claims break Google's guidelines.
- Rich results are never guaranteed, even with valid markup.
- Test markup with Google's Rich Results Test and the Schema Markup Validator after every change.

Q: What is schema markup in simple words?
A: Schema markup is hidden code on a web page that labels facts, such as your business name, address, hours, products or FAQs, using the standard schema.org vocabulary. Visitors never see it; search engines read it reliably, which helps them understand your page and can make it eligible for richer results.

Q: Which schema type should a local business use?
A: Use LocalBusiness or, better, the most specific subtype that fits, such as Dentist, Restaurant or Store, as Google's documentation advises. Include the required name and address, plus recommended opening hours and map coordinates, and make every detail match your visible page and Google Business Profile.

Q: Does schema markup improve Google rankings?
A: Not directly. Structured data helps Google understand your content and can make pages eligible for rich results, which may attract more clicks. Rankings still depend on helpful content, relevance, page experience and trust. Valid markup does not guarantee that Google will show a rich result.

Q: How do I test my website's schema markup?
A: Use Google's Rich Results Test to see which rich result types a page is eligible for and any errors, and the Schema Markup Validator for general schema.org checks. After launch, review the enhancement reports in Google Search Console, and retest whenever hours, prices or templates change.

Q: Can I add review stars with schema markup?
A: Only for genuine reviews that are visible on the page and allowed under Google's guidelines. Never mark up fake, self-written or hidden reviews. Google also restricts some self-serving review markup for businesses, so check its current review snippet documentation before adding review markup.

Q: Schema markup kya hota hai aur kya meri website ko chahiye?
A: Schema markup chhupa hua code hai jo search engines ko aap ka naam, pata, timings aur products saaf tareeqe se batata hai. Zyada tar businesses ko LocalBusiness, BreadcrumbList aur zaroorat ke mutabiq FAQPage ya Product chahiye. Isay Google ke Rich Results Test se check karein.

## Website Speed Optimization for Pakistani Mobile Users: What Actually Matters and Why
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-speed-pakistan-mobile
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: Website speed optimization for Pakistani mobile users means meeting Google's Core Web Vitals on real phones: main content visible within 2.5 seconds, taps answered within 200 milliseconds and no layout jumps above 0.1. Test on a mid-range Android phone over 4G, then fix images, hosting and heavy scripts first.
Key points:
- Speed matters because most Pakistani visitors browse on mid-range Android phones over mobile data.
- Google's Core Web Vitals measure loading (LCP), responsiveness (INP) and visual stability (CLS).
- Good thresholds are LCP 2.5 seconds or less, INP 200 milliseconds or less and CLS 0.1 or less, at the 75th percentile.
- Lab tests are a start; real-phone tests over 4G at busy times show what customers feel.
- The biggest wins usually come from images, hosting and third-party scripts, in that order.

Q: What are good Core Web Vitals scores?
A: According to web.dev, a good Largest Contentful Paint is 2.5 seconds or less, a good Interaction to Next Paint is 200 milliseconds or less, and a good Cumulative Layout Shift is 0.1 or less. Each should be met by at least 75% of real page loads, measured separately on mobile and desktop.

Q: How do I test my website speed on mobile in Pakistan?
A: Run PageSpeed Insights on the mobile setting, then test on a real mid-range Android phone over mobile data with the cache cleared, at busy times such as evenings. Lab tools run on Google's servers rather than in Pakistan, so your own phone tests show what local customers experience.

Q: Does website speed affect Google rankings?
A: Google uses page experience signals, including Core Web Vitals, as part of how it evaluates pages, though helpful, relevant content matters more. Speed has a clearer effect on customers: slow pages lose visitors before they read anything, especially on mobile data, which reduces enquiries and sales.

Q: What slows down most business websites?
A: In our experience, the usual causes are large uncompressed images, weak or overloaded hosting without caching, too many third-party scripts such as chat widgets and trackers, heavy themes and page builders, too many plugins and several web fonts. Test results show which of these matter most for your site.

Q: What is a speed budget for a website?
A: A speed budget is a limit agreed before building, such as a target LCP on a mid-range phone over 4G or a maximum page weight. Written into the project scope and tested before launch, it stops speed becoming an afterthought and makes trade-offs about heavy features explicit.

Q: Website ki speed kaise barhayen?
A: Pehle PageSpeed Insights aur apne Android phone par mobile data se test karein. Phir tasveerein chhoti aur compress karein, achhi hosting aur caching lein, ghair zaroori chat widgets aur scripts hatayen, aur halka theme istemal karein. Main content dhai second ke andar nazar aana chahiye.

## Website Gets Visitors but No Enquiries? A 12-Point Audit and the Fixes That Work
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-visitors-no-enquiries
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A website with visitors but no enquiries usually has 1 of 4 problems: the wrong visitors, contact options that are hard to find, too little trust, or a broken form. Check that forms and WhatsApp links actually work, put a call and WhatsApp button on every page, show prices and proof, and measure clicks before redesigning.
Key points:
- First check whether enquiries are being lost: test every form, email and WhatsApp link yourself.
- Visitors from irrelevant searches or cheap traffic will never enquire, however good the page.
- Contact options must be visible on every page, especially on phones.
- Prices, real photos, reviews and named people build the trust that turns visits into messages.
- Measure button clicks and form submissions, so you know what changed after each fix.

Q: Why does my website get traffic but no leads?
A: Usually one of four reasons: enquiries are being lost by a broken form or wrong WhatsApp link, the visitors are not potential buyers, contact options are hard to find on phones, or the page does not build enough trust. Test every form and button first, then check traffic sources and trust signals.

Q: How do I check if my contact form is working?
A: Submit it yourself from a phone and a computer and confirm the email arrives, including in spam. Ask someone else to test too. Forms often stop sending after hosting changes or plugin updates, so retest after any change, and consider sending a copy of each enquiry to a second inbox.

Q: Does adding a WhatsApp button increase enquiries?
A: Often, in Pakistan, because many customers prefer sending a WhatsApp message to filling in a form. Place Call and WhatsApp buttons in a fixed bar on mobile, use the international number format, pre-fill a short message and track clicks in Google Analytics to measure the effect.

Q: Should I show prices on my website to get more enquiries?
A: Usually yes. Starting prices or ranges filter out people who cannot afford you and reassure those who can, who are then more likely to contact you. Explain what changes the final price. Hidden prices make many visitors leave rather than ask, especially with businesses they do not know.

Q: How do I track enquiries from my website?
A: Set up events in Google Analytics for form submissions, WhatsApp button clicks and call button clicks. Google's recommended events include one for lead generation. Check them in the Realtime or DebugView reports after setting up, then compare enquiry numbers before and after each change you make.

Q: Website par log aate hain lekin rabta kyun nahin karte?
A: Pehle khud form aur WhatsApp button test karein ke kaam kar rahe hain ya nahin. Phir dekhein ke sahi log aa rahe hain ya nahin. Har page par call aur WhatsApp button rakhein, qeemat ka andaza dein, asli tasveerein aur reviews dikhayen, aur form chhota rakhein.

## WhatsApp Button on Your Website: Click-to-Chat Links, Pre-Filled Messages and GA4 Tracking
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/whatsapp-button-website-leads
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A WhatsApp button on a website uses a click-to-chat link: wa.me followed by your full international number without the plus sign, spaces or leading zero, such as wa.me/923284675162. Add ?text= with a URL-encoded message to pre-fill it, place the button in a fixed bar on mobile, and track clicks as a GA4 event.
Key points:
- Click-to-chat links open a WhatsApp chat with your number without the visitor saving it first.
- Use the full international number with country code, and no plus sign, dashes, spaces or leading zero.
- A pre-filled message tells you which page or product the customer came from.
- On phones, a fixed bar with WhatsApp and Call buttons works better than a small floating icon.
- Track button clicks in Google Analytics, so you know which pages bring conversations.

Q: How do I create a WhatsApp link for my website?
A: Use https://wa.me/ followed by your full international number, with the country code and no plus sign, spaces, dashes or leading zero. For a Pakistani mobile number such as 0328-4675162, that is wa.me/923284675162. Test the link on a phone after adding it to your website.

Q: How do I add a pre-filled message to a WhatsApp link?
A: Add ?text= to the end of the wa.me link, followed by your message encoded for web addresses, where spaces become %20 and commas %2C. Most website builders and plugins encode it for you. The visitor can edit the message before sending, so keep it short and helpful.

Q: How do I track WhatsApp button clicks in Google Analytics?
A: Send a GA4 event, such as whatsapp_click, when the button is clicked, using Google Tag Manager or an analytics plugin, with a parameter for the page. Confirm it in the Realtime report or DebugView, mark it as a key event, and review which pages produce the most clicks.

Q: Where should a WhatsApp button be placed on a website?
A: On phones, a fixed bar at the bottom of the screen with WhatsApp and Call buttons, visible on every page, works well. On desktop, place it in the header and beside each product or service. Avoid small floating icons hidden behind cookie banners or other widgets.

Q: Should I use WhatsApp Business app or the Business Platform?
A: The WhatsApp Business app suits small teams, with quick replies, labels and away messages on one number. Businesses with many chats and several agents can use the WhatsApp Business Platform through an approved provider, which supports shared inboxes and automated messages. Start with the app unless volume demands more.

Q: Website par WhatsApp button kaise lagayen?
A: Link aise banayein: wa.me/ ke baad apna number 92 se shuru kar ke, bina plus, zero, dash ya space ke, jaise wa.me/923284675162. Message pehle se likhne ke liye ?text= ke baad message lagayen. Mobile par neeche WhatsApp aur call ka button rakhein aur clicks Google Analytics mein track karein.

## Website Hacked: What to Do in the First 24 Hours, Step by Step
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-hacked-what-to-do
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: If your website is hacked, act in this order within 24 hours: put the site into maintenance or take it offline, change every password, tell your hosting company, restore a clean backup from before the hack, update everything, then check Google Search Console for security issues. Find how they got in, or it will happen again.
Key points:
- Contain first: stop the damage spreading to visitors before trying to fix anything.
- Change all passwords, including hosting, admin, database, FTP and email, from a clean device.
- Restoring a clean backup taken before the hack is usually the fastest reliable fix.
- Update WordPress, themes and plugins, and remove anything unused, before going live again.
- Check Google Search Console for security warnings and request a review once the site is clean.

Q: What should I do first if my website is hacked?
A: Contain the damage first: put the site into maintenance mode or ask your host to take it offline, and save screenshots of what you see. Then change every password from a clean device, turn on two-step login and contact your hosting company for logs and help.

Q: Can I restore my hacked website from a backup?
A: Usually yes, and it is often the fastest reliable fix, if you have a clean backup from before the hack. Restore from too late and the problem returns. After restoring, update everything, remove unknown users, change passwords and find how attackers got in before going live again.

Q: Why does Google say my site may be hacked?
A: Google flags sites where it detects malware, spam pages or other signs of compromise, to protect searchers. Check the security issues report in Google Search Console, clean the site, then request a review. Warnings are removed after Google confirms the site is clean, which can take some time.

Q: How do websites usually get hacked?
A: Common entry points are outdated plugins, themes or core software with known flaws, weak or reused passwords, pirated or nulled themes and plugins, shared logins and insecure hosting. Keeping software updated, using strong unique passwords with two-step login and avoiding pirated add-ons prevents most attacks.

Q: How much does it cost to fix a hacked website?
A: It depends on how badly the site is affected and whether a clean backup exists. We quote emergency clean-ups after a first look. Prevention costs much less: our maintenance plan at Rs 7,200 a month includes updates, off-site backups and monitoring, which stop most hacks before they happen.

Q: Website hack ho jaye to kya karein?
A: Sab se pehle website band karein ya maintenance mode lagayen, phir saaf device se tamam passwords badlein aur two-step login lagayen. Hosting company ko batayen, hack se pehle ka saaf backup restore karein, sab kuch update karein aur Google Search Console mein security warning check karein.

## Website Security Checklist for Small Businesses: 14 Checks You Can Do This Month
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-security-checklist-small-business
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A website security checklist for a small business covers 14 checks: updates for core, themes and plugins; strong unique passwords; two-step login; one account per person; removing old users; off-site backups; HTTPS; trusted plugins only; file editing disabled; and hosting, domain and email security. Review it monthly.
Key points:
- Most small business websites are hacked through outdated software, weak passwords or pirated add-ons, not targeted attacks.
- Updates, strong passwords with two-step login and backups prevent most problems.
- Give each person their own account with the least access they need, and remove it when they leave.
- Protect the accounts around the website too: hosting, domain registrar and email.
- A monthly 30-minute review, or a maintenance plan, keeps the checklist working.

Q: How do I secure my small business website?
A: Keep core software, themes and plugins updated, delete unused ones, use strong unique passwords with two-step login, give each person their own account with limited access, remove old users, keep off-site backups and test restores, use HTTPS everywhere and secure your hosting, domain and email accounts.

Q: How often should I update my WordPress website?
A: Check for updates at least monthly, and apply security releases as soon as they appear. WordPress's hardening guide notes that older versions are not maintained with security updates. Take a backup before updating, and test key pages and forms afterwards to catch any conflicts.

Q: Are free or nulled WordPress themes safe?
A: Free themes from the official WordPress directory are reviewed and generally safe. Nulled themes are pirated copies of paid themes, often shared on unofficial sites, and frequently contain hidden malicious code. They also receive no updates. Always buy paid themes and plugins from the official seller.

Q: Do I need two-factor login on my website?
A: Yes. WordPress's hardening guide recommends two-step authentication as an extra layer beyond passwords. Turn it on for the website admin, hosting, domain registrar and email accounts. Email matters most, because whoever controls your email can usually reset the passwords on every other account.

Q: Does a small business website need a maintenance plan for security?
A: Not if someone on your team reliably updates software, reviews access and checks backups every month. If not, a maintenance plan is cheaper than a hack. Ours costs Rs 7,200 a month and covers updates, off-site backups with restore tests, access reviews and monitoring.

Q: Website ko hack hone se kaise bachayen?
A: WordPress, themes aur plugins har maheene update karein, mazboot aur alag passwords ke saath two-step login lagayen, har bande ka apna account rakhein aur chhorne walon ka account foran hatayen. Backup server se bahar rakhein, kabhi nulled theme na lagayen, aur domain aur email ko bhi mehfooz rakhein.

## Website Down? A 10-Minute Check to Find the Cause and Know Who to Call
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-down-check
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A website down check takes about 10 minutes: first test on mobile data and another device to see if it is down for everyone, then check whether the domain or SSL certificate has expired, whether the hosting account is suspended or full, and whether a recent update caused an error. Each cause has a different person to call.
Key points:
- First confirm the site is down for everyone, not just your office network or browser.
- Expired domains and SSL certificates are among the most common and easiest causes to fix.
- Hosting suspensions often follow an unpaid invoice or a site using too many resources.
- A blank page or server error straight after an update usually points to a plugin or theme conflict.
- Knowing who controls the domain, hosting and code saves hours when something breaks.

Q: Why is my website not opening?
A: Common reasons are a problem with your own network, an expired domain, an expired or broken SSL certificate, a suspended or overloaded hosting account, or an error after a plugin, theme or software update. Test on mobile data and another device first, then check the domain, certificate and hosting in turn.

Q: How do I check if my website is down for everyone?
A: Open it on your phone using mobile data instead of Wi-Fi, try a different browser or private window, and ask someone in another city to open it. If it works for others, the problem is likely your network or browser cache rather than the website itself.

Q: What happens when a domain expires?
A: The website and email linked to it stop working, and visitors may see a parking page or advertisements. Registrars usually allow a grace period to renew, after which the domain may be released and registered by someone else. Renew immediately and turn on auto-renewal to avoid it happening again.

Q: What does a 500 error on my website mean?
A: A 500 error is a general server error, often caused by a plugin, theme or code problem, especially right after an update. Your developer can check the error log, disable the last changed plugin through the hosting file manager and restore the previous version to bring the site back.

Q: How can I get alerts when my website goes down?
A: Use an uptime monitoring service that checks your site every few minutes and alerts you by email or messaging when it stops responding. Many hosts and maintenance plans include monitoring. Combine it with auto-renewal for the domain and hosting, which prevents some of the most common outages.

Q: Website nahin khul rahi, kya karein?
A: Pehle mobile data aur doosre phone par check karein ke sab ke liye band hai ya sirf aap ke liye. Phir dekhein ke domain ya SSL ki muddat to khatam nahin hui, hosting ka bill ada hai ya nahin, aur kisi update ke baad error to nahin aaya. Har wajah ke liye alag shakhs se rabta karein.

## Website Redesign Without Losing Traffic: Redirect Maps and Google's Site-Move Steps
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/new-website-without-losing-google-traffic
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A website redesign without losing traffic depends on one document: a redirect map that sends every old address to its best new equivalent with a permanent 301 or 308 redirect. Google advises keeping redirects for at least 1 year, updating internal links and sitemaps, and expecting some ranking movement for a few weeks.
Key points:
- Most traffic losses after a redesign come from old addresses that no longer work, not from the new design.
- List every old URL that gets traffic or links, and map each one to its closest new page.
- Use server-side permanent redirects, and avoid sending everything to the home page.
- Google advises keeping redirects for at least one year after a move.
- Monitor Search Console and analytics closely for several weeks after launch.

Q: Will I lose Google rankings if I redesign my website?
A: Not necessarily. Most losses come from old page addresses that stop working. With a complete redirect map, permanent server-side redirects, unchanged or improved content on top pages and updated sitemaps, rankings usually settle after some fluctuation. Google notes that changes can take weeks or longer to settle.

Q: What is a redirect map?
A: A redirect map is a spreadsheet listing every old URL on your website and the new URL it should redirect to. It covers pages with search traffic, links from other sites or printed references. Pages with no equivalent should return a proper not-found response rather than redirect to the home page.

Q: Should I use 301 or 302 redirects when moving my website?
A: Use permanent redirects, 301 or 308, for a redesign or move. Google says permanent redirects signal that the new URL should be shown in results, while temporary ones, such as 302, keep the old URL as the main one. Server-side redirects are the most reliable.

Q: How long should I keep redirects after a website move?
A: Google's site-move guidance says to keep redirects for as long as possible, generally at least one year. Many businesses keep them indefinitely, because old links from other websites, emails and printed material keep sending visitors to the old addresses for years.

Q: Can I redirect all old pages to my new home page?
A: Avoid it. Google advises against sending many unrelated old URLs to one page such as the home page, because it treats them more like missing pages. Redirect each old page to its closest new equivalent, and let pages with no replacement return a not-found response.

Q: Nayi website banwate hue Google traffic kaise bachayen?
A: Purani website ke har page ka address aur us ka naya address aik list mein likhein aur 301 redirect lagayen. Sab ko home page par na bhejein. Launch par naya sitemap Search Console mein dein aur kuch hafte errors check karte rahein. Redirects kam az kam aik saal rakhein.

## Website Slow on Mobile? How to Find the Cause and Fix It, Step by Step
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-slow-on-mobile
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: If your website is slow on mobile, run PageSpeed Insights on the mobile setting and test on a real Android phone over mobile data. The usual causes, in order, are oversized images, weak hosting without caching, too many plugins or scripts, and heavy fonts. Aim for main content within 2.5 seconds; fixing images alone often halves page weight.
Key points:
- Diagnose before changing anything: PageSpeed Insights plus a real phone test over mobile data.
- Oversized images are the most common cause and the cheapest to fix.
- Slow server response points to hosting, caching or database problems rather than design.
- Every plugin, widget and tracking script adds weight; remove what you do not use.
- Fix one thing at a time and retest, so you know what worked.

Q: Why is my website slow on mobile but fine on desktop?
A: Phones have slower processors and mobile data has more delay than office broadband, so heavy pages hurt more. Many sites also send phones large desktop images, sliders and scripts. Test with PageSpeed Insights on the mobile setting and on a real phone over mobile data to see what is slowing it.

Q: Do too many plugins slow down WordPress?
A: They can. Each plugin may add scripts, styles or database queries to every page, and poorly built plugins add more. Delete plugins you do not use, replace several small ones with one well-built plugin where possible, and retest after each change to see the effect.

Q: How do I make images load faster on my website?
A: Resize images to the size they are displayed, compress them, use modern formats such as WebP or AVIF, and lazy-load images below the first screen. Photos taken on phones are often several megabytes each and should never be uploaded directly without resizing.

Q: Will better hosting make my website faster?
A: If the server response is slow, yes. PageSpeed Insights flags slow server response times. Turning on caching, adding a CDN, or moving to a better plan or host near your visitors can help significantly. If the problem is large images or scripts, hosting alone will not fix it.

Q: How fast should my website load on mobile?
A: Google's Core Web Vitals treat a Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less as good, measured across real page loads. In practice, aim for the main content to appear within about two and a half seconds on a mid-range phone over mobile data.

Q: Website slow kyun hai aur kaise theek karein?
A: Aam tor par wajah bari tasveerein, kamzor hosting, zyada plugins aur chat ya tracking scripts hoti hain. Pehle PageSpeed Insights aur apne phone par mobile data se test karein. Tasveerein compress karein, caching lagayen, faltu plugins aur scripts hatayen aur har tabdeeli ke baad dobara test karein.

## Website Backup Guide for Small Businesses: How Often, Where to Store It and How to Test
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-backups-small-business
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A good website backup plan copies both files and database, weekly for a small brochure site and daily or more often for online stores, keeps at least 3 copies with 1 stored away from your hosting, and is tested by actually restoring it. Always take a backup before any update.
Key points:
- A complete backup includes the website files and the database; one without the other is not enough.
- Back up weekly for small, rarely changed sites and daily or more for stores and busy sites.
- Follow the 3-2-1 idea: three copies, on two kinds of storage, with one away from your host.
- Take a backup before every update, plugin install or major change.
- Test a restore regularly; an untested backup may not work when you need it.

Q: How often should I back up my website?
A: WordPress's guidance suggests weekly backups for smaller sites and daily backups for busy ones, plus a backup before every upgrade. Online stores and booking systems usually need daily backups or more, because orders and bookings change constantly and are difficult to recreate once lost.

Q: What is the 3-2-1 backup rule?
A: It is a common rule of thumb: keep at least three copies of your data, on two different kinds of storage, with one copy off-site. For a website, that might be the live site, your host's backups and a separate copy in cloud storage you control.

Q: Are my hosting company's backups enough?
A: Often not on their own. Host backups may be stored on the same server, kept for only a few days, or lost if the account is hacked or suspended. Keep at least one additional copy in storage you control, and check how long the host keeps backups and how to restore them.

Q: What should a website backup include?
A: A complete backup includes the website files, such as themes, plugins, images and uploaded documents, and the database, which stores pages, posts, products, orders, users and settings. A backup missing either part cannot fully restore the site, so check that both are included.

Q: How do I know my website backup works?
A: Test it. Every few months, restore a backup to a staging copy of the site and check that pages, images, forms and orders work. WordPress's guidance also recommends occasionally taking a manual backup to confirm the automated process is running properly.

Q: Website ka backup kaise aur kitni dafa lein?
A: Chhoti website ka har hafte aur online store ka rozana backup lein, aur har update se pehle bhi. Backup mein files aur database dono hon. Kam az kam teen copies rakhein, jin mein se aik hosting se bahar apne cloud account mein ho, aur kabhi kabhi restore kar ke test zaroor karein.

## How Long to Build a Website? Realistic Timelines by Website Type and What Delays Projects
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/how-long-to-build-a-website
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: How long to build a website depends on its type: about 1 week for a landing page, 2 to 3 weeks for a 5-page site, 3 to 5 weeks for a 10-page business site, 4 to 8 weeks for an online store and 6 weeks or more for a web app. Missing content and slow feedback cause most delays.
Key points:
- Typical timelines run from about a week for a landing page to several months for a large web app.
- The build itself is rarely the slowest part; content, photos and approvals usually are.
- Online stores take longer because of product entry, payments and courier set-up.
- A written scope with milestones and dates makes the timeline visible to both sides.
- You can speed things up by preparing content early and naming one person to approve work.

Q: How long does it take to build a small business website?
A: With content ready and quick feedback, a website of up to 5 pages typically takes 2 to 3 weeks with us, and a business website of up to 10 pages 3 to 5 weeks. Missing text and photos or slow approvals are the most common reasons projects take longer.

Q: How long does it take to build an online store?
A: Typically 4 to 8 weeks. Store projects take longer than ordinary websites because products, sizes and photos must be entered, and payments, delivery charges and couriers set up and tested. Payment gateway approvals can take longer than the build itself, so apply early.

Q: How long does a web application take to develop?
A: A focused first version of a web app often takes six weeks or more, while larger systems with several user roles and integrations take several months. Building in phases, starting with the core workflow, gets a usable version live sooner and lets real use guide the next phase.

Q: Why do website projects get delayed?
A: Most delays come from the client side rather than coding: missing content and photos, slow or conflicting feedback, new features added mid-project, and third-party approvals such as payment gateways. Preparing content early and naming one decision-maker prevents most of them.

Q: Can a website be built in 3 days?
A: A simple template site can go online in days if content is ready and little customisation is needed. A full custom site, store or web app in a few days usually means skipped steps, such as phone testing, security and backups. Compare what each quote includes, not only the deadline.

Q: Website kitne din mein banti hai?
A: Landing page taqreeban aik hafte mein, 5 page website 2 se 3 hafton mein, 10 page business website 3 se 5 hafton mein aur online store 4 se 8 hafton mein banta hai. Web app mein 6 hafte ya us se zyada lagte hain. Sab se zyada der text, tasveeron aur approval mein hoti hai.

## What Pages Does a Small Business Website Need? Page Lists by Industry and What Each Must Say
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/pages-for-small-business-website
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: Most small business websites need 5 core pages: home, services or products, about, contact, and a privacy policy. Then add pages by industry, such as doctor profiles for a clinic or product categories for a manufacturer. A 5-page site starts from Rs 40,500; most growing businesses need up to 10 pages, from Rs 85,500.
Key points:
- Every business website needs a home page, services or products, about, contact and a privacy policy.
- Give each main service or product line its own page, so customers and search engines find it.
- Industry needs differ: clinics need doctor profiles, shops need delivery and returns pages, manufacturers need catalogues.
- Each page should answer one set of customer questions and end with a clear next step.
- Start with the pages customers need now; add guides and extras once the core is strong.

Q: What pages should a small business website have?
A: At minimum: a home page, a services or products page, an about page, a contact page with map, hours and WhatsApp, and a privacy policy. Most businesses then add one page per main service or product line, plus industry-specific pages such as doctor profiles or delivery and returns.

Q: How many pages should a business website have?
A: Many small businesses start with five core pages and grow to around ten, adding a page for each main service and a frequently asked questions page. The right number is the number needed to answer customers' main questions clearly, not a fixed target.

Q: Do I need a separate page for each service?
A: Usually yes, for your main services. A separate page can answer specific questions, show relevant photos and prices and appear in searches for that exact service. A single page listing everything gives customers and search engines much less to work with.

Q: What should an about us page include?
A: Your story and how long you have operated, the people behind the business with photos, your premises, the registrations or certifications you genuinely hold, and why customers choose you. Keep it factual and specific; trust comes from details customers can verify, not general claims.

Q: Does a small business website need a privacy policy?
A: If your website collects personal information through forms, bookings, orders or analytics, a privacy policy explaining what you collect and how you use it is good practice and may be required where your customers live. Ask your adviser what applies to your business.

Q: Business website mein kaun se pages hone chahiye?
A: Har business website mein home, services ya products, about, contact aur privacy policy ke pages hone chahiye. Phir har bari service ka alag page banayein. Clinic ke liye doctors ke profiles, dukan ke liye delivery aur return ka page, aur manufacturer ke liye products ka catalogue zaroori hai.

## Website Accessibility Basics for Business Owners: A 10-Point WCAG Checklist in Plain English
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-accessibility-basics
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: Website accessibility basics mean making your site usable by people with disabilities, following the W3C's Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG). Start with 10 checks: alt text, headings, contrast, keyboard use, visible focus, labelled forms, clear links, captions, readable text sizes and no content that relies on colour alone.
Key points:
- WCAG, from the W3C, is the common reference for web accessibility, with levels A, AA and AAA.
- Its four principles are that content must be perceivable, operable, understandable and robust.
- Ten basic checks catch many common problems and also make sites clearer for everyone.
- Accessible sites often work better for search engines, because structure and text alternatives are clearer.
- Some laws require it: Ontario sets WCAG 2.0 Level AA for public sector bodies and firms employing 50 or more people.

Q: What is WCAG?
A: WCAG stands for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, published by the W3C. They set out how to make web content accessible to people with disabilities, organised around four principles, perceivable, operable, understandable and robust, with success criteria at Levels A, AA and AAA. WCAG 2.2 is the current version.

Q: Which WCAG level should a business website aim for?
A: Most organisations aim for Level AA, which covers the most important barriers without the very strict requirements of Level AAA. Some laws name a specific version and level; for example, Ontario requires WCAG 2.0 Level AA for covered organisations. Check what applies in your market.

Q: Does website accessibility help SEO?
A: Several accessible practices also help search engines understand your pages: clear heading structure, descriptive alt text, meaningful link text and real text instead of text inside images. The main reason to do it is your customers, but better structure benefits search visibility too.

Q: Is website accessibility required by law?
A: It depends on your location and size. In Ontario, designated public sector organisations and businesses or non-profits with 50 or more employees must make public websites meet WCAG 2.0 Level AA. Other countries have their own laws and guidance, so take local legal advice for your markets.

Q: How can I check my website's accessibility quickly?
A: Run Lighthouse in Chrome for an automated report, then try using the site with only a keyboard, zoom to 200% and test the home and contact pages with a free screen reader. Automated tools catch only some problems, so these manual checks are essential.

Q: What is alt text and why does it matter?
A: Alt text is a short written description of an image that screen readers read aloud and that appears if the image fails to load. Meaningful images need it so blind users understand the content; decorative images should be marked so screen readers skip them. Search engines also use alt text.

## Website Launch Checklist: 40 Checks to Run Before Your Website Goes Live
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-launch-checklist
Updated: 2026-10-29
Short answer: A website launch checklist should cover 40 checks in 8 groups before going live: content, SEO, speed, security, forms and contact, tracking, legal pages, and backups and ownership. Run it on a phone and a laptop, fix every failure, then repeat the key checks within 1 week after launch.
Key points:
- Most launch problems are small and avoidable: broken forms, wrong numbers, leftover test content and blocked indexing.
- Group the checks so different people can own content, technical and business items.
- Test on a real phone over mobile data, not only on the developer's computer.
- Confirm that domain, hosting, analytics and admin accounts are in the owner's name before launch.
- Recheck forms, indexing and speed in the first week after going live.

Q: What should I check before launching a website?
A: Check content for placeholders and wrong details, SEO basics such as indexing and titles, mobile speed, HTTPS and updates, every form and WhatsApp link, analytics and Search Console, privacy and policy pages, and that backups exist and the domain, hosting and admin accounts are in your name.

Q: Why do forms often fail after a website launch?
A: Forms that worked on staging can fail on the live site because email settings change with the domain or hosting, or messages land in spam. Submit every form after launch, check that emails arrive, including in spam folders, and consider sending a copy of each enquiry to a second address.

Q: How do I make sure Google can index my new website?
A: Switch off any search engine blocking left on during development, remove stray noindex tags, submit an XML sitemap in Google Search Console and inspect key pages there. A week after launch, check the indexing report for errors and fix any pages Google cannot index.

Q: Should I take a backup before launching my website?
A: Yes. Take a full backup of files and database just before launch and store it away from the server. Make sure automatic backups are scheduled for the live site and test one restore, so you can recover quickly if anything goes wrong in the first weeks.

Q: Who should own the domain and hosting at launch?
A: The business owner. Before launch, confirm that the domain and hosting are registered in your name with your email, that you have admin logins to the website, analytics and Search Console, and that your developer is added as a separate user you can remove later.

Q: Website launch se pehle kya check karein?
A: Launch se pehle dekhein ke koi demo text na ho, qeematein aur phone number sahi hon, har form aur WhatsApp button kaam kare, website mobile par jaldi khule, HTTPS ho, Search Console aur Analytics set hon, privacy policy ho, backup liya gaya ho aur domain aur hosting aap ke naam par hon.
